column2: All tribes come to Hebron and declare their kinship in bones and flesh, retaining behold and ordinary address to David.
Past leadership under Saul and the quoted divine promise preserve leading out/in, shepherding and rulership; divine My and human you are distinguished.
All elders, covenant before the Lord and anointing over all Israel remain, including the repeated Hebron location.
Thirty years of age and forty years of reign remain in the sentence continued by the separate reign durations.
Seven years and six months in Hebron over Judah and thirty-three in Jerusalem over Israel and Judah remain; no arithmetical smoothing is supplied.
The Jebusite inhabitants, denied entry and blind/lame resisting and speaking remain the selected sequence.
column3: The quoted/narrated boundary is editorial; no claim about literal disability, an idol identification or another witness's unless construction is inserted.

column2: David captures Zion's stronghold, identified as his city; the parenthetical identification is not made a new act of naming.
Dagger, lame, blind and those hating David's soul remain in the attack command, followed by the selected Lord's house saying.
column3: Attack construes haptomai in its hostile context. The difficult coordination and reference of the groups remain open; a water shaft and an alternative who-is-hated relation are not substituted.

column2: Dwelling, city designation, building around from the citadel and David's house remain; no named Millo is supplied.
Greater and greater expresses the progressive growth construction; the accompanying Lord Almighty remains its stated context.
Hiram of Tyre sends messengers, cedar and both wood and stone workers, who build David a house.
David recognizes preparation for kingship and elevation of the kingdom for his people Israel.
column3: The final his can refer to David or the Lord; lowercase inherited his is not an editorial resolution of that antecedent.

column2: Additional wives and concubines from Jerusalem after Hebron, and additional sons and daughters, remain; daughters are not omitted before the male-name list.
The opening four Jerusalem names retain Shammua, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon as inherited forms of the selected list.
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg and Japhia continue the same list without imposed harmonization with Chronicles.
Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet remain before the additional lettered list; the verse is not treated as the end of all stored names.
All thirteen names of the extra unit remain, from Samae to Eliphalath, including repeated Nathan and separately spelled related forms.
column3: This record preserves the selected sequence, not an accepted reconstruction of which individuals or duplicate traditions the two lists represent.

column2: All the foreigners seek the newly anointed David, who hears and descends to the stronghold; the two directions and agents remain distinct.
Valley of the Titans retains the translated selected designation rather than replacing it with Rephaim.
David's two questions retain direct divine Wilt Thou and the answer's emphatic certainly; human your in God's reply remains ordinary.
From the Upper Breaches, the strike there, water comparison and repeated place-name preserve the selected direction and wordplay.
column3: The inherited active waters break through construes the middle/passive water comparison idiomatically; precise hydraulic imagery remains open.

column2: The foreigners abandon their gods, which David and his men take; burning or destruction is not added.
Again is supported by the added/repeated ascent construction; the Valley of the Titans remains the gathering point.
The second inquiry receives a prohibition against meeting them directly, a turning command and approach near the place of weeping.
column3: The place designation is not silently replaced with a tree species or fixed geography.

column2: The grove's closing-together sound, descent, the Lord's preceding action and battle with the foreigners remain.
column3: The sound/constriction expression is unresolved; marching in treetops and an identified tree species are not supplied as though present in this Greek.

column2: David obeys and strikes from Gibeon to Gezer's land, retaining both selected endpoints.
Again and approximately seventy thousand young men preserve the repeated gathering and the selected count rather than thirty thousand.
The ascent from Judah's rulers, ark, invoked name of the Lord of hosts and cherubim enthronement remain.
column3: The rulers/ascent wording and final above it relation are compressed; no place-name correction or architectural reconstruction is credited.

column2: The new cart, Abinadab's hill house and Uzzah with his brothers as drivers remain; the singular initial subject is contextual David, not a newly named operator.
With the ark continues the preceding cart clause, while Uzzah's brothers go before it; no singular Ahio replaces the plural brothers.
Celebration, tuned instruments, strength, songs and the five instrument classes remain.
column3: Lyres and harps are working identifications of kinyrai and nablai, not a documented organological resolution; no wood-species phrase replaces tuned instruments.

column2: Nodab, outstretched hand, grip, bull calf pulling aside and repeated hold it fast remain.
column3: The final purpose infinitive's attachment is difficult and remains open; it is not deleted as redundancy or replaced by a different account of the animals stumbling.

column2: The Lord's anger, God's strike, death beside the ark and before God remain; an unstated explanation of Uzzah's offence is not added.
David's disheartenment remains distinct from the preceding divine anger, with breach wordplay and the named memorial to the narrator's day.
David fears the Lord and asks how the ark can come to him; no implied answer is inserted.
Unwillingness to bring the covenant ark to David's city precedes its diversion to Obed-edom the Gittite's house.
Three months and blessing of the whole household and all possessions remain; the ark itself is not made the grammatical agent of blessing.
The reported blessing because of God's ark motivates David's bringing up the Lord's ark with gladness; both titles remain.
Seven dancing companies carrying the ark and the sacrificial calf and lamb remain the selected construction.
column3: The relation of the companies to the bearers remains a syntactic question; no six steps, additional oxen or fattened animal is imported.

column2: David's playing on tuned instruments and distinctive robe remain rather than a linen ephoud or a substituted dancing-only account.
David and all Israel's house bring up the ark with shouting and trumpet sound, preserving the collective agency.
Michal's window view, David dancing and playing, and contempt within her heart remain distinct from his visible conduct.
Ark placement inside David's pitched tent and his whole burnt and peace offerings remain; no permanent temple is implied.
The completion of both offering classes precedes blessing in the name of the Lord of hosts.
The full Dan-to-Beersheba force, men and women, each portion and three bread/cake descriptions remain before household dispersal.
column3: The hearth and pan preparations are retained without changing them to meat or raisin cakes; exact culinary identifications remain provisional.

column2: David's return to bless, Michal's stated blessing and her accusation of exposure before servants' servant women remain, including the dancer comparison.
column3: Blessed is the selected narrative verb even if her following speech is ironic; the translation does not silently change it to cursed.

column2: David promises dancing, blesses the Lord and recalls selection above Michal's father and his house, then repeats celebrating and dancing before the Lord.
Further uncovering and worthlessness in your eyes retain direct address to Michal and the difficult connection to the servant women and honour.
column3: The final coordination and relative clause remain unresolved; honour among them is not turned into an uncomplicated opposite of Michal's contempt by importing another reading.

column2: Michal's childlessness through the day of her death remains without a supplied cause, punishment mechanism or later exception.
